description: Open specification for cryptographic agent authorization in commerce — a layered SD-JWT credential format that creates a tamper-evident delegation chain proving an AI agent's actions were within human-delegated scope. Maintained by Mastercard; open to multi-stakeholder contribution.
agents: Not an agent platform — defines the authorization credential standard that agent platforms must implement
SD-JWT delegation chain: credential provider → user → agent
Two modes: Immediate (user reviews final values) and Autonomous (user sets constraints, agent acts independently)
Constraints cryptographically bound: amount range, allowed merchants, product line items
Checkout-payment integrity binding: cryptographic proof that payment mandate references same checkout the user approved

pp_fit.feature: PP is the enforcement and receipt layer that VERIFIES Verifiable Intent credentials at execution time. VI defines the credential format; PP issues the authorization receipt confirming the agent acted within the VI-defined scope.
pp_fit.integration_complexity: medium — spec-level alignment needed; PP would implement VI credential verification and issue receipts against VI's delegation chain
pp_fit.urgency: high — draft v0.1 just published, window to engage during standard-setting phase is now
pp_fit.strategic_angle: CRITICAL: PP should contribute to this spec and position as the reference enforcement implementation. If VI becomes the commerce standard for agent authorization (backed by Mastercard's network), PP being the canonical receipt-issuer is a platform-level win. This is not a sales target — it's a standards play.

spec_details.explicitly_out_of_scope_note: The spec leaves enforcement/receipt issuance undefined — that is PP's exact wedge

competitive_overlap: None — VI defines what was authorized; PP proves what was executed. Complementary primitives.
